texts: good. the whenever rule fires: a crowd of nightmoths gathering at a lantern-row is the trigger, and the descending sky-cats plus the purpose "to hunt" all ride the per-occurrence result.
good. the rule is fireable, "a handful" is kept as a count phrase rather than invented as a number, and the sky-cats staying on the cliff-spires is tied to the gathering it accompanies.
good. "the Keepers" stays one named actor, the crowd rule is the thing used, and "for generations" lands as a span of at least two generations.

bad: "in one night" was recorded as the eating itself lasting a night, which the sentence does not say, and the per-night rate — the actual point — is lost; there is no operator for "within a span of". Rewrite it as a plain nightly habit: "Each sky-cat eats many nightmoths every night." — "every night" parses as a nightly recurrence, "many nightmoths" keeps its vague count, and the one-cat reading survives in the "each".

good. it fires as a rule — a sky-cat hunting at a lantern-row triggers a fall in that row's thread harvest, ordered after the hunt. One softness: the harvest is created inside the result, so it exists only where a hunt happens.
good. the crowd is one group of nightmoths, the recovery is predicated of that crowd, and "slowly" is kept as the manner.
